x: Last year, at our first time of competing, we managed to share the trophy with the London A.C., but with the Blackheath H. sending up a strong side, which included Sidney Wooderson, we were not too optimistic this time.

Wooderson's 800 metres record is worth 1109 points as against 1088 due to Lovelock's 1500 metres in Berlin. Rather surprisingly the "worst" record is the 10,000 metres recently put up by Maki, which scores 1075 points.
Wooderson, with Len Marchant 3rd and Alf Orton 4th. Bill Lucas won the mile, and Shrubb was 3rd.
A good turn out and a good crowd—mainly to see Wooderson. A good race with Carter in his unbeatable mood; and a 30-points margin in our team win.
Wooderson ran well to beat Les. Cohen, although the latter was just back from a week's holiday.

This time was three seconds faster than Wooderson's schoolboy record, and compares favourably with the schoolboy times of American stars, such as Cunningham's 4m. 24.7s., MacMitchell's 4m. 21.1s., Dodds' 4m. 28.4s., Lash's 4m. 30.5s., and Zamperini's 4m. 21.2s.
At the Blackheath Harriers Open Meeting our team was third in the Invitation 2 Miles, in which Sydney Wooderson attempted to lower the British Record.

After a terrific struggle Vern. was barely a yard ahead of Reid at the change over, with Wooderson some distance in the rear. On to the foot of Dale Hill, about 4¾ miles, Len Herbert was never comfortable and eventually finished 35 secs. behind the Stagbearers.
